links.why: A clause cannot be joined to itself. The waw of cl0 joins the next clause, cl1, which is kept below.
Plain waw (וְ) between two clauses describing the earth and then the darkness; no cause, result or purpose.
Plain waw (וְ) before the spirit clause, which has its own subject; the sense is additive.
R1: 'And God said' introduces what is said, 'Let there be light'. The saying clause links to the said clause as well as the turn's frame and part.
Direction reversed. The narrative runs from the saying clause (cl0) to the clause after it (cl2); 'it was light' follows 'God said', it does not precede it.
cl1 is inside the speech, and the narrative line does not continue from inside a speech. What came of the command is recorded as its result instead.
wayyiqtol cl2 continues the narrative line from the nearest clause before it that is not inside a speech, the saying clause cl0.
A jussive command, then waw + wayyiqtol saying what came of it ('and it was light'). This is the effect of imp1.

groups.why: God is the speaker ('God said'). The turn holds the saying as frame and the commanded words as part.
'part' is not a member role of the imperative kind. cl2, 'and it was light', is what the command brings about, so it is the group's effect.

cant_tell.why: The text names no one to whom God says 'let there be light'; the words are a jussive with no named addressee.

links.why: כִּי after the verb of seeing: 'he saw that the light was good'. The clause is what God saw, the object of the verb, not a reason.
Direction reversed. The narrative runs from the seeing (cl0) to the separating (cl2); cl2 does not precede cl0.
wayyiqtol cl2 continues the narrative line from the seeing in cl0. The that-clause cl1 is the object of that seeing, not a speech, and does not break the line.

cant_tell.why: The field holds a parser code (o010010040051), not a conjunction. The כִּי appears in the gloss as 'that', so the that-link is decided from the gloss.

referents.why: Third masculine singular implied subject of cl1 ('he called night'). In the same verse cl0 has God as the one calling, and the act of naming is God's.
referents.category: implied subject continuing the same agent

links.why: Reversed. 'And it was evening' follows the calling clauses; it does not precede cl0.
Plain waw (וְ) joining two namings by the same agent; no cause, result or purpose.
wayyiqtol cl2 continues the narrative line from the nearest clause before it that is not inside a speech, cl1.
wayyiqtol cl3 ('and it was morning') continues the narrative line after the evening.

cant_tell.what: whether cl0 and cl1 form an acts group
cant_tell.why: Both are acts of God, but the subject is stated by name only in cl0. The acts pattern requires the subject to be stated only in the verb, so it is not proposed.

cant_tell.what: attachment of the verbless cl4 'day one'
cant_tell.why: It names the day made up of the evening and the morning (cl2 and cl3 together). The form does not settle whether it elaborates cl3 alone or the pair.
